explain.say: Zoroastrianism is one of the oldest living religions. It began in ancient Iran with the prophet Zarathustra, called Zoroaster in Greek. Scholars debate when he lived, with guesses from about 1500 to 500 BCE.

draw.label: Ancient Persia, and the Parsi community of India

explain.say: Zarathustra taught that there is one wise and good God, Ahura Mazda, the Wise Lord. Against goodness stands a destructive spirit, Angra Mainyu, and every person must choose which side to follow.
The whole faith is summed up in three principles: good thoughts, good words, good deeds. Choosing good helps goodness win in the end.
Zoroastrians pray before a sacred fire in fire temples. The fire is not worshipped itself: it is a symbol of God's light, warmth and purity, and some temple fires are kept burning for centuries.

draw.text: Fire: a symbol of purity and the light of God

explain.say: The holy book is the Avesta. Its oldest part, the Gathas, are hymns believed to be Zarathustra's own words. Children join the faith in a ceremony called the navjote, receiving a white shirt and a sacred cord.

Zoroastrianism was the faith of great Persian empires. After the Arab conquest of the 600s CE, many followers moved to India and became the Parsis. Today the community is small, perhaps 100,000 to 200,000 people.

items: about 1500 to 500 BCE: Zarathustra, dates debated
224 to 651 CE: the Sasanian Empire, official faith

faq.q: What are the three Zoroastrian principles?
faq.a: They are good thoughts, good words and good deeds, in the ancient Avestan language Humata, Hukhta and Hvarshta. Zoroastrians believe that by living this way each person helps goodness triumph.
asks: What is good thoughts good words good deeds?

faq.a: Zarathustra, called Zoroaster in Greek, was the prophet who founded Zoroastrianism in ancient Iran. Zoroastrians believe he received a vision of one wise God, Ahura Mazda. Scholars are unsure when he lived, with estimates from about 1500 to 500 BCE.

Ahura Mazda, meaning Wise Lord, is the one supreme God of Zoroastrianism, wholly good, the creator of truth, light and life. Zoroastrianism is often described as one of the world's oldest religions that teach one God.
asks: What do Zoroastrians believe about God?

faq.a: No. Zoroastrians pray in the presence of fire, but they do not worship the fire itself. Fire is a symbol of God's light, energy and purity, much as other faiths use candles or lamps.
asks: Why do Zoroastrians pray before fire?

faq.q: What is the Zoroastrian holy book?
faq.a: It is the Avesta. Its oldest and most sacred part, the Gathas, are seventeen hymns believed to come from Zarathustra himself. The Avesta is written in Avestan, an ancient Iranian language.

The Parsis are Zoroastrians whose ancestors left Persia after the Arab conquest and settled in western India more than a thousand years ago. Many live in Mumbai, and the community is known for its contributions to business, science and charity.
asks: Why are there Zoroastrians in India?

faq.a: The Faravahar is a well known symbol linked with Zoroastrianism: a winged disc with a human figure. It is often explained as a reminder of the three principles and the soul's journey towards goodness.

A navjote is the ceremony that welcomes a child into the Zoroastrian faith, usually between about 7 and 15. The child receives a white shirt, the sudreh, and a sacred cord, the kusti, tied around the waist during daily prayers.
asks: What is a sudreh and kusti?

faq.a: Nowruz, meaning new day, is the Persian new year at the spring equinox, around 21 March. It has ancient Zoroastrian roots and is celebrated by Zoroastrians and many millions of others in Iran, Central Asia and beyond.
asks: What is the Persian new year?

faq.q: What did Zoroastrians believe about the afterlife?
faq.a: Zoroastrians believe the soul is judged after death, crossing a bridge that is wide for the good and narrow for the wicked. They also believe that in the end goodness will win and the world will be renewed.
asks: What happens after death in Zoroastrianism?

faq.q: What are the Towers of Silence?
faq.a: In the past many Zoroastrians placed the dead on open stone towers, called dakhmas, where birds returned the body to nature, so as not to pollute earth or fire, which they hold sacred. Today many communities use burial or cremation instead.
asks: How do Zoroastrians treat the dead?

faq.a: The community is small, with estimates of about 100,000 to 200,000 people. Most live in India and Iran, with growing communities in North America, Britain and Australia.

Many scholars think Zoroastrian ideas, like a final judgement, heaven and hell, and good struggling against evil, may have influenced later religions in the region. Others are more cautious, and the question is still studied.

facts: Zarathustra is called Zoroaster in Greek; scholars estimate he lived somewhere between about 1500 and 500 BCE.
The Zoroastrian name for God is Ahura Mazda, meaning Wise Lord.
The Zoroastrian holy book is the Avesta; its oldest part is the Gathas.
Zoroastrianism was the official religion of the Sasanian Empire, from 224 to 651 CE.
The Parsis of India are descendants of Zoroastrians who left Persia after the Arab conquest.
